doc.title: Chazz Frichtel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 13, 2016

title: First trip to Los Angeles with Rebop Kwaku Baah
summary: Carmen Caramanica brought him on a project for Rebop; he cut three of his songs and was drawn to move.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Yeah. Playing here in the years that I did before I went to L.A. was just priceless. And I told Carmen yesterday, because Carmen pulled me in on a project in L.A. before I moved there. It was centered around a percussionist who played in the group Traffic. And his name was Rebop Kwaku Baah. He was a Nigerian prince percussionist. And Carmen had gotten a call from a piano player who was a guy that was Lou Rawls’ music director, Reg Powell, and a drummer, Jack Toker, lives in Seattle. And Reg was kind of putting this thing together for Rebop for Island Records or something. So somewhere along the way Carmen said, “hey, I know this bass player guy, I’ll bring him with me.” So that was my © Fillius Jazz Archive -13-

first trip to L.A. And that was, whoa, eye opening on so many levels. As it turned out Rebop kind of disappeared. So to try and salvage, we had a few days left, two or three days left. Carmen had heard a couple of my original tunes and he says, “why don’t you play these for the guys?” So I played three songs of mine. And Reg said, “Let’s see if we can get some studio time at Conway Studios.” Which is still operating in L.A. We went in and cut three songs. And then we all went home and Reg and a lawyer friend of his started to shop the tape and we got some interest I think from A&M and maybe Reprise or something. And Reg was saying to me, because I was checking in with him, how’s it going, and I had already started, I felt the pull of the Pacific. And so he said, “man maybe you want to come out here.” And I thought well yeah, maybe so. So I did.
